audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers rendered different level charts. Full: Akali/Akali/Akali/Skill/Akali/Skill/Skill. Content and packet: Anivia/Anivia/Akali/Skill/Anivia/Akali/Anivia. Five of seven rows disagreed.
audit.why: Five Point Strike is 550 range and costs 110 mana at rank 1; Akali has no dash at all until Shuriken Flip at level 3. Anivia's Flash Frost is 1075. Levels 1-2 are Anivia's. Level 3 flips to Akali when the 825-range flip lands. Level 6 goes back to Anivia because Glacial Storm denies her the ground she needs and Perfect Execution is 120s at rank 1; the first-item row flips to Akali when her AP lands.
audit.corrected: Full-layer phases[0,1,4,6].side and phases[5].side flipped to match the content layer and packet; phases[N].why rewritten to match each new owner.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text named a nonexistent ability ('Shuriken/Vitality Twin dash') and pinned the first-item swing to Rylai's for Anivia and 'a lethality spike' for Akali.
audit.why: Akali's abilities are Assassin's Mark, Five Point Strike, Twilight Shroud, Shuriken Flip and Perfect Execution. She builds AP, not lethality. Anivia's first-item spike is her mana item, which is what keeps Glacial Storm running.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3].text rewritten with real names and real cooldowns: Shuriken Flip 16s at rank 1, Twilight Shroud 20s, Perfect Execution 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was absent: Shuriken Flip marks a target and re-casts into a DASH along that line, and Crystallize creates impassable terrain — a wall on that line denies both her entry and her return. The page also called Twilight Shroud a dash and claimed it gave sustain.
audit.why: Anivia W flag: 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Akali E flag: 'dash — mobility that grounding and walls can deny'. Twilight Shroud in Riot's text grants move speed and untargetability, no healing. Assassin's Mark is an auto-attack reset with bonus range — per _missing, the wind-up is the tell, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: Wall-versus-flip written into breakdown.carry, breakdown.late, late, dosFull[1], spikes[3]; the auto-reset tell written into breakdown.feeding and dontsFull[2]; the false Shroud sustain removed from wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers, only the instruction to count.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud 20/19/18/17/16s, Shuriken Flip 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Perfect Execution 120/90/60s, Crystallize a flat 17s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written in with what each window buys.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] advised buying anti-heal 'early into his sustain'. Akali's kit contains no heal.
audit.why: Assassin's Mark, Five Point Strike, Twilight Shroud, Shuriken Flip and Perfect Execution have no healing in Riot's text and no heal flag in the kit file.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal line replaced with the Zhonya's answer to Perfect Execution.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer referred to Akali as 'his'/'him'/'HIM' throughout.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed across tldr, winCon, loading, phases whys, dosFull, dontsFull and report entries.

edits.before: Anivia's Crystallize wall is one of the best anti-Akali tools in the game — split her escape route or block her all-in path — and paired with Glacial Storm zoning she becomes far more punishable in teamfights, giving you control of the game's second half.
edits.after: Crystallize is terrain and the Shuriken Flip recast is a dash, so a wall on that line strands her — no entry and no exit. Paired with Glacial Storm chill doubling every Frostbite, her assassination angles stop working and the game's second half is yours.
